attempts.summary: On node1, added /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/10-complexity.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3. pam_pwquality was already wired into /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth via authselect, so no PAM stack changes were needed. Verified enforcement with real passwd changes as a non-root test user (boundary tests: 11 chars/3 classes rejected, 12 chars/1 class rejected, 12 chars/3 classes accepted, 14 chars/4 classes accepted), confirmed by unchanged vs. changed shadow hashes. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id and healthy system state, issued `systemctl reboot` via a detached background command so the ack returned first, polled until the node reconnected, confirmed the boot_id changed, confirmed the policy file and PAM wiring persisted, and re-ran the weak/strong password enforcement test post-reboot with the same pass/fail results. All test users were removed afterward.
